results.identification: A condensed summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2024 General Election manifesto—‘Change: Labour Party Manifesto 2024’—and its accompanying ‘Six First Steps for Change’ pledge card, as published by the Labour Party in June 2024.
results.evidence: The text explicitly opens with “Labour’s 2024 manifesto” and is structured around Labour’s “five national missions.” It names signature Labour policies and language from 2024: Great British Energy (£8.3bn), a National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn), Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn), “Make Brexit work” (no single market/customs union/FoM), the New Deal for Working People (zero‑hours/fire‑and‑rehire), a cap on corporation tax at 25%, no rises in NI/Income Tax/VAT, abolishing non‑dom status, ‘First steps for change’ (six first steps: NHS waits, Border Security Command, Great British Energy, antisocial behaviour, 6,500 teachers, economic stability).

results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the UK Conservative and Unionist Party’s 2024 General Election manifesto ('Clear Plan. Bold Action. Secure Future.'), i.e., the Conservative Party manifesto published in June 2024.
results.evidence: References to distinct Conservative 2024 pledges: 'Triple Lock Plus' for pensions; mandatory National Service at 18; monthly Rwanda removals and an annual legal migration cap; defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; 'Backing Drivers Bill' (incl. ULEZ reversal measures, 20mph/LTN referendums); clarifying that sex means biological sex in the Equality Act; implementing the Cass Review; two SMR approvals within 100 days; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; and the overarching 'secure future' framing with five pillars.

results.identification: A condensed summary of Reform UK’s 2024 General Election manifesto titled ‘Our Contract with You,’ produced by the Reform UK party (UK), i.e., content from their 2024 manifesto/contract document.
results.evidence: “Reform UK’s 2024 ‘Contract with You’ presents a rapid-change programme…” plus explicit platform planks unique to Reform UK such as “Freeze non‑essential immigration and ‘stop the boats.’”, “Scrap Net Zero policies…”, “leave the ECHR if needed”, “Employer immigration tax”, “20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance”, “Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs/most 20mph zones”, and the section header “Funding (party estimates)”.

results.identification: An unofficial bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2024 General Election manifesto (“For a Fair Deal”), derived from the party’s manifesto document rather than being the manifesto itself.
results.evidence: The header says "Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)" and the text opens with "Core promise: A Fair Deal..." (the Lib Dems’ 2024 strapline). It lists signature Lib Dem policies such as "Proportional representation (STV)", "rejoin key programmes (Horizon, Erasmus)", "Net zero by 2045", "ban no‑fault evictions", and "votes at 16"—all consistent with the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2024 general election platform.

results.identification: A third‑party bullet‑point summary of the Green Party of England and Wales’ 2024 UK General Election manifesto (Real Hope, Real Change), derived from the party’s official manifesto and costings but not an official document itself.
results.evidence: The heading explicitly says “Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary.” The bullet points match signature Green Party of England & Wales positions: no new oil and gas, oppose nuclear and cancel Trident, public ownership of rail and water, proportional representation and votes at 16, Right to Roam, rent controls and ending Right to Buy, frequent‑flyer levy and banning short domestic flights with 3‑hour rail alternatives, path to rejoin the EU with free movement, wealth tax and 10:1 pay ratio cap, four‑day week, and nationalising the Big 5 retail energy suppliers.

results.identification: A neutral, bullet‑point summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2024 General Election manifesto (“Change”), published by the Labour Party in June 2024.
results.evidence: Distinctive Labour 2024 pledges appear throughout: “five missions” incl. clean power by 2030; creation of Great British Energy (HQ in Scotland) capitalised with £8.3bn; a £7.3bn National Wealth Fund; restoring the 2030 petrol/diesel car phase‑out; bringing rail into public ownership as contracts expire; no new North Sea oil and gas licences; the New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero‑hours, end fire‑and‑rehire, day‑one rights); building 1.5m homes with reintroduced mandatory targets and ‘grey belt’ releases; Warm Homes Plan with £6.6bn; Border Security Command; votes at 16; Lords reform (remove hereditary peers, retirement at 80); stay outside the EU but seek a veterinary agreement/MRAs/touring fix and a security pact; 700,000 urgent NHS dental appointments; ban trail hunting and badger cull; Ukraine support incl. repurposing frozen Russian assets.

results.identification: A neutral, bullet‑point synopsis of the UK Conservative and Unionist Party’s 2024 General Election manifesto (and associated policy plans), derived from that manifesto.
results.evidence: Includes signature 2024 UK Conservative Party pledges: "Mandatory National Service at 18"; "Rwanda removals with monthly flights"; "Triple Lock Plus" for pensions; cutting employee NI to 6% and abolishing the main self‑employed NI rate; "Back Drivers Bill" incl. reversing London ULEZ expansion; clarifying the Equality Act to define sex as biological; reallocating £36bn from HS2 phase 2; Help to Buy return; 40 hospitals by 2030; legal annual cap on work and family visas; consent‑led onshore wind and new nuclear at Wylfa.

results.identification: A condensed, third‑party-style summary of Reform UK’s 2024 UK general election manifesto (branded by the party as ‘Our Contract with You’), drawn from Reform UK’s published manifesto and costings document.
results.evidence: The heading explicitly says "Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Summary (policy proposals and costings only)" and the content matches Reform UK’s 2024 manifesto (‘Our Contract with You’) policies and figures, e.g. raising the income tax threshold to £20,000, leaving the ECHR, an employer immigration tax (NI 20% on foreign workers), scrapping Net Zero policies, 40,000 more police officers, corporation tax cut to 20% then 15%, abolishing IR35, and the funding line "Savings: £150bn p.a. + £10bn p.a. from assumed extra growth = £160bn p.a.; Costs: £141bn p.a."

results.identification: A de‑jargonized bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2024 General Election manifesto (“For a Fair Deal”), i.e., their official manifesto policies presented in neutral wording.
results.evidence: Distinctive Liberal Democrat policies appear throughout: replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; proportional representation via STV for MPs; scrapping Police & Crime Commissioners; strong pro‑EU stance (rebuilding ties now and seeking Single Market membership long‑term, Erasmus+ return, veterinary/mutual recognition deals); ending the Rwanda plan and the Illegal Migration Act; 380,000 homes per year including 150,000 social homes; net zero by 2045 with 90% renewable electricity by 2030; new water regulator and sewage crackdown; free personal care and a Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); right to see a GP within 7 days and +8,000 GPs; raising the Digital Services Tax to 6%; arts in the EBacc; BBC/Channel 4 protections; and PR, Lords reform, votes at 16, and scrapping voter ID.

results.identification: An unofficial bullet‑point summary of the Green Party of England & Wales 2024 General Election manifesto (UK), derived from the party’s manifesto rather than being the manifesto text itself.
results.evidence: The heading explicitly says “Summary of key proposals (Green Party Manifesto 2024).” The policies are UK‑specific and align with the Green Party of England & Wales: NHS and social care funding, scrapping tuition fees, building 150,000 social homes, protecting the Green Belt, Council Tax revaluation, public ownership of rail/water/energy retailers, ending Trident and signing the TPNW, PR voting and Lords reform, EU re‑entry/Erasmus, and UK‑specific terms like Crown Estate, MoJ, DEFRA, and Right to Roam.
